historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors

starting.description: Researchers observed uptake inhibition by established tricyclic antidepressants and certain antihistamines, then pursued greater serotonin selectivity; a separate Lundbeck line developed an observed active noradrenaline-inhibiting phthalane and related compounds, some with dual uptake effects, into citalopram.

inspiration.description: The observed pharmacology and clinical use of existing synthetic antidepressants, observed monoamine-uptake inhibition by synthetic antihistamines, and uptake effects of the Lundbeck phthalane/talopram compound series.

steps.description: Carlsson recalls serotonin-uptake inhibition by clinically used tricyclics and by less-selective antihistamines.
His group selected brompheniramine and chlorpheniramine, and Corrodi developed the structurally related selective inhibitor zimelidine.
In a parallel Lilly program, diphenhydramine observations led to related compounds; comparative assays and structural changes yielded fluoxetine as a potent selective serotonin-uptake inhibitor.

In the Lundbeck branch a melitracen-related synthesis unexpectedly produced an active phthalane; analogue design yielded the noradrenaline-selective talopram, while related compounds showed dual uptake inhibition.
Lundbeck redirected work toward selective serotonin uptake inhibition, producing citalopram; escitalopram is the active S-enantiomer of citalopram.

design.description: Chemists altered antihistamine-related compounds and compared uptake activity across variants. In the Lundbeck branch, an unanticipated change from a tricyclic to a phthalane architecture was followed by analogue design and a change in uptake selectivity, from noradrenaline toward serotonin; the S-enantiomer of citalopram was later isolated.

circumstances.description: S4 describes an unexpected phthalane product and noradrenaline-uptake finding in the Lundbeck precursor work; the later Lundbeck serotonin-selective search and Lilly's comparative selective-uptake screening were deliberate. S5 classifies the SSRIs, including citalopram, as non-serendipitous without discussing the precursor events. The extent of chance across accounts is unresolved.

limits: The Swedish zimelidine and Lilly fluoxetine programs developed separate chemical series from prior observations; neither establishes chemical descent for all cohort members.
The citalopram/escitalopram line is a distinct phthalane branch with its own active precursors; S4 is a secondary account dependent on a Lundbeck history, not independent verification.
Paroxetine and sertraline are within the supplied class boundary but their individual development lineages were not traced; do not extrapolate a particular chemical precursor to every member.
conflicts: S4 reports an unexpected citalopram-precursor structure and uptake effect, whereas S5 places citalopram in a discovery category excluding chance. S5 does not address those precursor events; the scope or reason for the discrepancy is unresolved. The approved observation-led category does not require accidental discovery.

S5 calls fluoxetine first synthesized/developed but says zimelidine was first introduced. S1 compares a zimelidine patent date with Lilly's first uptake test, not the same milestone as synthesis. Precise synthesis priority remains unresolved.

Carlsson speculates that zimelidine's eventual clinical success might have influenced other companies; Wong and colleagues state that they did not initially know about the Swedish team's new-inhibitor development. The accounts address different time periods and do not establish either a contradiction or that fluoxetine was derived from zimelidine.
gaps: The full Carlsson–Lindqvist 1969 paper was unavailable during collection; only its abstract was read.
The original Wong and colleagues 1974 fluoxetine paper was available only as an indexed publisher abstract, not full text; its abstract was not used as a historical causal account.
The Bøgesø–Sánchez Lundbeck discoverer chapter and Hyttel's 1977 citalopram original were located but not read beyond publisher metadata, section headings, or references.
Contemporaneous records needed to settle exact first-synthesis and the disputed role of chance in the Lundbeck precursor were not compared in full.

humanContributionInterpretation.summary: Tricyclic clinical benefits and unwanted cardiac or anticholinergic effects motivated more selective antidepressant work.
humanContributionInterpretation.scope: Serotonin-uptake assays were central; this is a successor-development rationale rather than a new observed clinical signal.
